title: Prove the exact full-guard header law for laminar projector families (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

A scoped counting proof gives the exact joint full-guard header law for any laminar family of idempotents over every finite field. A laminar family has nested projectors and orthogonal siblings. Its joint fraction is

```text
for each node v, including an unguarded ambient root:
    multiply the orthogonal-family law inside im(v) for its children
```

The new lemma is that Schur deletion preserves containment. Together with #4246's orthogonality lemma and law, it gives the product and an exact binary-field obstruction at any saturated even branch. At q=3,m=3, a rank-one projector inside a rank-two projector passes jointly on 343/1404 of headers; independent marginals give 931/4563.

The [advance claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19082877) named the nested rank-one/rank-r case. The same containment lemma proves the more general laminar result delivered here. Claim type: scoped proof with finite corroboration. No new κ or supplier admission. Only `research/laminar-header-law/` is added.

## Evidence

Before, #4246 left nonorthogonal full-guard families open. The new written argument covers nesting and arbitrary-depth laminar families. The direct census checks 213,714 headers and every one of 1,056 laminar coordinate families across eight domains over F2,F3,F4,F5. All fractions and zero criteria agree. It checks 181,836 Schur-containment cases in both directions, plus six controls. An explicit nonnested commuting pair has noncommuting Schur complements, so that larger class requires a different argument. The stdout receipt is generated and binds every package file by SHA256.

From the repository root, any CPython 3.12 may replace this interpreter:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -B research/laminar-header-law/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -O -B research/laminar-header-law/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/laminar-header-law
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/laminar-header-law --check-source-history
```

Expected markers: `PASS_LAMINAR_HEADER_LAW`, `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE ... outcome=completed`, and `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES`.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

The universal claim is the written proof using the cited orthogonal-family theorem, not a proof-kernel result. The finite census reaches m=4 over F2 and m=3 over F3/F4. General overlapping commuting or noncommuting families, prime-power rings, incomplete/weighted covers and adaptive requests are outside scope. Header selection, emission, dispatch, dirty return, stock and actual producer/caller costs are unpriced. No selected cold replay or formal build is run. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

## Open next questions

1. Classify the changing Schur pair for two rank-two commuting projectors in dimension three with nonnested overlap. The explicit noncommuting Schur witness identifies the missing invariant.
2. Pin one actual laminar request producer and fully price its shared-header caller. The count alone supplies no physical saving.

## Related open work

- #4246, head `a2d99d73bf21b39fbb0a9a88917424ff26c2e63c`: orthogonal arbitrary-rank law, used as a cited theorem. This package adds nesting and tree composition. Its flat rank-(2,1) example at q=3,m=3 is 14/117 here, agreeing numerically with the published value. No proof audit is claimed.
- #4240, head `9f9c89ed75e9fdae6b6762925b080fb308824858`: nonorthogonal rank-one families at the first pivot. Distinct higher-rank/full-chain question here. Its equal-projector rank-one value at q=3,m=2 is 7/12; this package's single rank-one count agrees numerically.
- #4239, head `5e24dfb5463d540721687d92c369609da5589523`: orthogonal rank-one law. Its q=3,m=2,k=2 example gives 1/6, agreeing numerically with this census's corresponding flat family.
- #4228, head `bb25dcedb5bbbacd3c35359eb6b5488b087bcde6`: single-request all-rank law and Schur deletion, cited steps. Its q=3,m=3,r=2 fraction is 49/117, agreeing numerically with this census's single rank-two case.
- #4227, head `3d793eade8de2ba49ec08f8d004c1b2f566a78e6`: extreme-rank marginal laws. Its q=3,m=2 rank-one fraction is 7/12, agreeing numerically with this census; no new marginal result is claimed.
- #4261, head `4728fc766b3084f3ab2f5c8543a5e74e4a12b126`: concurrent overlapping corank-one pair law. That pair is neither nested nor orthogonal when m>2, so it is outside this laminar theorem. Its common flat q=3,m=2 boundary is 1/6, agreeing numerically with this census. Its count does not classify the changing Schur pairs asked about in this package's first open question.
- #4215: retained good-packet normal form. Different algebraic question, no shared aggregate count compared.
- #4100: the proposed BIT request/complete-header context. This package derives a joint counting law; it does not audit or admit that construction, and no recursive bill or κ is shared.

## CI notes

Local environment: macOS 27.0.1 arm64, CPython 3.12.15. Warnings are errors in both registered modes. No standalone Ruff executable was available; code diagnostics used Python warnings and AST inspection.

Local metadata, both registered mathematical checks, and the five-file committed-byte/source-history preflight pass at `2a582d8f66d1900b22ee2cd0062ee5dca94e8f85`. The final registered two-command replay took 156.13 seconds total; each command was below that total and its 300-second limit. Separately timed direct normal and optimized commands took 44.99 and 61.70 seconds. These are check durations, not performance comparisons. No local obligation was delegated to CI. [Hosted run 39504972933](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/39504972933) is green on the same exact head: `plan` passed in 4m10s and the package `replay` passed in 3m20s. Both complete hosted receipts equal the local receipts, including every package-file SHA256 and all mathematical fields. The helper suite reports 312 tests, 11 skipped. Both registered normal/optimized checks and `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE ... outcome=completed` are present in the hosted log. No check failed and no registered obligation remains unrun.

## Merge danger

Two-way door. Blast radius is the isolated research package. No selected-frontier change.

This package was produced by Nick Petalas. It builds on Nick Petalas's #4228/#4239/#4240/#4246 and Cinna Davis's #4100 request context. Apache-2.0.
